story: The Governor directed the Texas Water Development Board to penalize data center water reporting failures, and the grid operator put the board's water questions into a request due October 12th.

claims.text: On September 14th, 2026 the Governor directed the Texas Water Development Board to force major water users including data centers to comply with water use reporting. The same directive imposes legal consequences for past and future failures.
claims.quote: Governor Greg Abbott today directed the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) to compel major water users, including data centers, to comply with water use reporting requirements and to impose legal consequences for past and future failure to comply with state law.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: The Governor's office states that major water users including data centers appear to have already committed civil and criminal violations by not giving the water board the required usage information.
claims.quote: Major water users, including data centers, appear to have committed civil and criminal violations through failure to provide TWDB with required information about water usage.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: The Governor framed the directive as a shared obligation, saying data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water.
claims.quote: "Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water," said Governor Abbott.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026
claims.note: The page uses straight double quotation marks. The quote reproduces the full sentence including the attribution clause.

claims.text: The Governor instructed the board to use its enforcement authority against past failures as well as future ones.
claims.quote: The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026
claims.note: This is the interior of the Governor's quoted statement. The first person pronoun belongs to the source and is never carried into published copy.

claims.text: The press release states that the board writes the state water plan and can't do that job while it is denied detail on existing and anticipated water consumption.
claims.quote: TWDB is charged with developing a state water plan that meets the needs of Texans and cannot perform that task if it is denied detailed information on existing and anticipated water consumption.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026
claims.note: This sentence is the Governor's office characterizing the board's position. It is not a statement issued by the board, and copy must not attribute it to the board.

claims.text: A data center that does not complete and return the water board's survey commits an offense punishable as a crime.
claims.quote: A data center that fails to complete and return the survey commits an offense punishable as a crime.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: A data center that misses the survey deadline also loses eligibility for TCEQ permits, amendments and renewals under Chapter 11 of the Texas Water Code.
claims.quote: A data center that fails to timely complete and return the survey is ineligible for TCEQ permits, amendments, or renewals under Chapter 11 of the Texas Water Code.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: The board was told to enforce those remedies, including referring noncompliant data centers to the County or District Attorney and notifying TCEQ for possible permit disqualification.
claims.quote: TWDB must enforce those remedies against noncompliant data centers, including referral to the appropriate County or District Attorney and notice to TCEQ for possible permit disqualification.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: This builds on an August 3rd, 2026 directive ordering the utility commission and the grid operator to audit every data center advancing through the interconnection process.
claims.quote: On August 3, 2026, Governor Abbott directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and ERCOT to conduct a comprehensive audit of all data centers that advance through ERCOT's interconnection process.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: The board must report back to the Office of the Governor on its enforcement progress by October 14th, 2026, with further updates after that.
claims.quote: TWDB shall update the Office of the Governor by October 14, 2026, on the progress of its enforcement activities, with further updates thereafter, including when the audit is complete.
claims.document: Office of the Texas Governor press release, Governor Abbott Directs TWDB To Penalize Data Center Reporting Failures, September 14th, 2026

claims.text: The same day, the grid operator issued a market notice carrying its own number and pairing the data center impact request with the water board partnership.
claims.quote: M-B091426-01 Issuance of Request for Information Regarding Data Center State and Community Impacts
claims.note: The notice number and the opening of its subject, taken contiguously from the notice type field. The page also renders a second form of the subject in its short description, where the same clause reads Regarding rather than Related to. Neither was tidied and this quote stops before the divergence.

claims.text: The request is aimed at developers of data centers 25 MW and larger, along with transmission and distribution service providers and market participants.
claims.quote: Developers of Data Centers 25 MW and Larger, Transmission and/or Distribution Service Providers, and Market Participants
claims.note: This is the intended audience field. The notice body limits the actual recipients to two defined groups and does not say every developer at or above 25 MW receives one. Copy may say the request is aimed at them. It may not say every one of them gets it.

claims.text: The water questions in Section C are asked on the water board's behalf under its Executive Administrator's authorization, and the answers are forwarded back to the board.
claims.quote: The Executive Administrator of the TWDB has authorized ERCOT to issue the questions in Section C on TWDB's behalf, and ERCOT will forward the responses to these questions to TWDB.

claims.text: Under Texas Water Code 16.012, a recipient that does not fully answer Section C may face criminal penalties.
claims.quote: In accordance with Texas Water Code 16.012, any failure to fully respond to the questions in Section C may subject an RFI recipient to criminal penalties and other potential consequences.
claims.note: The verb is may subject, so copy must not state criminal penalties as automatic.

claims.text: Responses are due at 5 p.m. Central Prevailing Time on October 12th, 2026.
claims.quote: 5 p.m. Central Prevailing Time (CPT) on October 12, 2026
claims.note: The action required block writes the same hour as 5pm CPT, unspaced and without periods. Both forms are on the page and neither was tidied.

claims.text: A complete response has to carry a notarized attestation from the data center developer.
claims.quote: a notarized attestation from the data center developer

claims.text: Failing to answer the request, or any part of it, is reported to the utility commission and the Office of the Governor.
claims.quote: Failure to respond to the RFI or any part thereof will be reported to the PUC and the Office of the Governor.

claims.text: This request is separate from the Batch Zero eligibility request issued on September 9th, 2026, which carries its own response obligation.
claims.quote: This RFI is separate from the Batch Zero Eligibility RFI issued on September 9, 2026.

claims.text: The grid operator expects to publish a report on what the responses show no later than December 10th, 2026.
claims.quote: ERCOT expects to publish this report no later than December 10, 2026.

claims.text: The August 3rd directive's scope names cooling technologies and water sources and consumption among the data center impacts the operator and the commission were told to gather.
claims.quote: including information about public financial assistance, dependency on grid power, water sources and consumption, cooling technologies, noise, light and traffic impacts, and ownership and controlling interests, among other topics
claims.note: This is the notice describing the earlier letter's scope. It is what lets a frame draw cooling plant. It does NOT say any particular data center uses any particular cooling method, and no frame may say so.

claims.text: The September 14th letter told the water board to partner with the operator on water consumption, water supply sources and water-efficient technologies.
claims.quote: partner with ERCOT to audit water consumption, sources of water supply, and implementation of water-efficient technologies
claims.note: The notice quoting the Governor's letter. The letter itself carries no extractable text layer this run, so its wording reaches this file only as the notice reproduces it.

rejected.finding: The Governor's underlying letter to the water board
rejected.reason: The press release link is a safelinks wrapper around a redirect. The file resolves and fetches as real PDF but carries no extractable text layer in this environment, so no page of it could be read. No quote was taken from it and none was invented. Its wording reaches this file only where the ERCOT notice quotes it.
rejected.why: PDF fetched but not parseable to text this run.

rejected.finding: That the request goes to EVERY data center developer of 25 MW and larger
rejected.reason: The audience field is broader than the body's recipient definition. The body restricts recipients to two defined groups, an interconnecting large load entity conditionally classified in Batch Zero that has not energized at 60 kV or above, and a developer of at least 25 MW but less than 75 MW classified as a Substantiated Load that has not energized at any voltage. Copy may say the request is aimed at developers 25 MW and larger. It may not say every one of them receives it.
rejected.why: The audience field is broader than the body's recipient definition.

rejected.finding: That data centers have largely not returned the water board's survey
rejected.what: any share or count of unreturned surveys
rejected.reason: Neither page publishes a count, a share or any quantity of returned or unreturned surveys. The strongest statement available is that major water users appear to have committed violations through failure to provide the information. Largely, most, and any figure standing for them are unquotable and are cut rather than approximated.
rejected.why: No count or proportion appears on either page.

rejected.finding: Attributing the state water plan sentence to the water board itself
rejected.reason: The sentence appears in the Office of the Governor's press release and is that office characterizing the board's position. No statement issued by the board was fetched this run. Copy carries it as what the press release states and never as the board speaking.
rejected.why: Wrong actor. The sentence is the Governor's office, not the board.

rejected.finding: That an incomplete Section C answer carries criminal penalties as a certainty
rejected.reason: The notice reads may subject an RFI recipient to criminal penalties and other potential consequences. The modal is load bearing and was not tidied away. Copy may say criminal exposure is attached. It may not say penalties follow.
rejected.why: The source says may subject, not will.

rejected.finding: Any figure for how many developers were sent the request, or how much water is at issue
rejected.reason: Neither page publishes a recipient count, a gallons figure, a megawatt total or any water consumption quantity. The only numerals in this file are those inside the verified quotes. Nothing was summed, converted or rounded.
rejected.why: No such number appears on either page.

rejected.finding: What any individual Section C question asks
rejected.reason: Section C of the request itself was not fetched. Only the notice's description of it is verified here, so no claim states what any individual question asks.
rejected.why: Section C itself was not fetched.

rejected.finding: That any particular data center uses evaporative cooling, or any stated cooling method
rejected.reason: The sources name cooling technologies and water-efficient technologies as subjects the audit asks about. Neither states what any data center actually uses. A frame may draw cooling plant as the thing being asked about. No frame may assert how a data center cools.
rejected.why: The sources name cooling as a question, never as a finding.

notes: Both source pages were re-fetched live on 2026-09-19 by the fact-checker and independently by the showrunner. Both returned full body text.
Every quote in this file was additionally checked character for character by the showrunner against its own fetch of the same page.
